business.title: Global Uranium Corp. Announces Conversion of Convertible Debentures
business.description: CALGARY, Alberta, Aug. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Global Uranium Corp. (CSE: GURN | OTC: GURFD | FRA: Q3J0) (the 'Company') is pleased to announce that the holders of the Company’s outstanding unsecured convertible debentures (the 'Debentures”) have elected to convert an aggregate of $670,100 of principal, together with accrued interest, into units of the Company (the 'Units”) in accordance with the terms of the Debentures.

business.title: Iovance Biotherapeutics Reports Inducement Grants under NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
business.description: SAN CARLOS, Calif., Aug. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: IOVA) ('Iovance' or the 'Company”), a biotechnology company focused on innovating, developing, and delivering novel polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte ('TIL”) therapies for patients with cancer, today announced that on August 20, 2026 (the 'Date of Grant”), the Company approved the grant of inducement stock options covering an aggregate of 240,135 shares of Iovance’s common stock to twenty new, non-executive employees.

science.title: The Milky Way may have merged with another galaxy shortly after the Big Bang
science.description: Since its formation, the Milky Way has merged with other galaxies, contributing to its current shape and composition. But recently, astronomers have found evidence of another merger that occurred shortly after the Big Bang.

science.title: Human microbes might be able to survive on the Moon’s South Pole. Here’s what that means for Artemis missions
science.description: A new study from NASA says certain pockets of the lunar South Pole — where the United States is expected to establish a moon base — may be sustainable for certain microorganisms. It could be a foundation for new lunar research, but it does bring its own challenges to future studies.

science.title: NASA-led study shows some Earth microbes could survive on the moon
science.description: The moon is, to put it mildly, an inhospitable place for people and other living organisms from Earth, with its lack of breathable air, extreme temperatures and exposure to relentless space radiation and energetic particles. That is why astronauts wear spacesuits and spacecraft are built with shielding.

science.title: What happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole turns off? These dying radio galaxies could show us
science.description: Astronomers have discovered a hitherto unseen population of galaxies with fading radio lobes, revealing what happens to these vast outflows when their black hole engines stall.

science.title: Lunar Quests, Space Ventures, and Mysteries of the Cosmos
science.description: The compilation of recent scientific updates includes China's ambitious Chang'e-7 lunar mission to discover moon ice, Muon Space's substantial funding elevation, breakthroughs in understanding narwhal tusks, concerns over satellite proliferation affecting astronomy, the USA's increased commercial space launches, the possibility of microbes surviving on the moon, and China's burgeoning space tourism.

science.title: Super-resolution microscopy reveals how a cancer drug triggers cellular breakdown
science.description: Cancer drugs are often designed to block specific molecular targets, but what happens after they enter a cell is not always well understood. A new study published in Biophotonics Discovery demonstrates how advanced imaging technology can help answer that question.
